criteriaNotes.0_hash_check: pixel_sha256 computed from object_gate for all five PNGs in /tmp/fsrooms/gate-r35; hashes recorded per item.
criteriaNotes.1_topdown_view: All five are 3/4 (top faces as planes + front faces), no side/iso faces. Brazier rim ellipse and foot top face read correctly; riser/steps are front faces under the dais top.
criteriaNotes.2_style_fit: Brazier uses the exact harbour stone brazier ramp (7513/7514). Riser pieces use a pale stone ramp matching the dais. Steps use the same ramp but with long flat fills and no joints, standing out from the jointed riser.
criteriaNotes.3_readability_1x: Brazier reads as laid fuel ready to light (crossed logs, cut ends, charcoal). Dais reads as raised with a front face in both rooms. Steps read weakly - lower step squashed (1px face), top tread merges with the lip.
criteriaNotes.4_placement: Brazier grounded by drop shadow; riser L/centre/R tile seamlessly and meet the dais border; steps join the riser on the left but the right stub joint at x30 breaks the 8px joint rhythm.
criteriaNotes.5_silhouette_outline: No stray pixels or stubs on the brazier outline; riser ends closed by dark outline columns. Minor: brazier row 11 ash pixels interrupt the inner front-rim line.

items.name: 큰 돌 화로(꺼짐, 2칸, 버들항 돌) (great stone brazier)
items.reasons: 3/4 correct: elliptical rim top (rows 2-12) seen from above, front faces of bowl, column (rows 19-22, cylindrical 6-step ramp) and foot (top face rows 24-25, front rows 26-29); no side/iso face. Palette is exactly the harbour stone brazier ramp (tiles 7513/7514): same slate blues, charcoal (26,14,6), bark (99,49,11)/(154,84,53), pale cut ends (208,196,182)/(185,171,157). At 1x and 3x in mock-gate the bowl reads as laid fuel: two crossing logs with light cut ends at x7-8/x21-22 row 5 over dark charcoal - ready to light, not an empty urn. Grounded by the 70-alpha drop shadow rows 30-31. Minor notes, not blocking: the ash (100,92,84) is mid-grey rather than pale, so the ash bed is weaker than the brief; row 11 x11-15/x18-20 ash pixels break the inner front-rim line; bowl has heavy horizontal banding (rows 13/15/18 dark bands) that reads as carved rings.

items.name: 돌 단 앞 턱(가운데, 1칸) (dais riser stone)
items.reasons: Rows 0-3 transparent so the dais top shows; row 4 light edge (200,208,208), row 5 lip, two stone courses (rows 6-9, 11-13) with joints at x5/x13 and x1/x9 staggered by 4 and tiling on an 8px rhythm across the 16px seam, dark line row 14, shadow row 15. In both mocks the pale dais clearly reads as a raised slab with a front face. Courses are flat-filled except for joints, acceptable for the smooth pale dais stone it extends.

items.name: 돌 단 앞 턱(왼쪽 끝, 1칸) (dais riser stone L)
items.reasons: Same rows as the centre piece with a dark outline column x0 and a lit edge column x1 (rows 5-13); course joints x5/x13 and x9 keep the centre rhythm so L|centre joins seamlessly. Left end meets the dais border cleanly in mock-gate and mock-vault.

items.name: 돌 단 앞 턱(오른쪽 끝, 1칸) (dais riser stone R)
items.reasons: Mirror of L without a highlight on the shaded side (dark outline x15 rows 4-14), consistent with left lighting; joints continue the centre rhythm; right end closes cleanly against the dais border in both mocks.

items.name: 돌 단 오르는 두 계단(2칸) (dais steps stone)
items.reasons: Reads only weakly as two steps and stands out against the jointed riser. (a) Unequal step faces: upper face rows 7-9 (dark line + 2px of (119,125,134)) but lower face is just the dark line row 13 + 1px row 14, so the bottom step looks squashed into a slat. (b) Treads x4-27 rows 5-6 and 11-12 and faces rows 8-9 and 14 are 24px-wide perfectly flat fills; next to the riser's staggered stone courses they look like smooth metal bars or a bench, not cut stone. (c) The top tread rows 4-6 is almost indistinguishable from the neighbouring riser lip (rows 4-6), so at 1x only one step reads. (d) Right outer stub x30-31 rows 12-13 puts a course joint at x30, off the riser's 8px joint rhythm (next tile joint at x33, 3px away). FIXES: re-profile rows 4-14 as tread1 rows 4-5 (edge+1), face1 rows 6-8 (dark nosing row 6 + 2px), tread2 rows 9-11 (light edge row 9 + 2px), face2 rows 12-14 (dark nosing row 12 + 2px), so both faces are 2px; add stone joints to each step face (e.g. face1 at x11/x20, face2 at x7/x16/x24, staggered) and a few (146,151,158)/(200,208,208) chips or a mid-tone wear strip on the tread centres so treads are stone, not flat bands; darken the cheek returns at x3/x28 one step on tread1 rows 4-5 so the cut reads recessed below the dais lip; move/remove the x30 joint in rows 12-13 so the right stub matches the riser rhythm (no joint, or put it where a riser tile would have it).
